provider_if_inherited: Website builder vendor; payment processor; POS app vendor
implementation_statement: The vendors provide account functions. The owner holds the only administrator account in the online store and the merchant portal. Gap: the owner and the family member share one POS app PIN, and nobody reviews which accounts and add-on connections exist.
evidence: Online store user and add-on list; POS app user list; merchant portal users

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner holds every duty, so duties cannot be separated. The family member is to use a separate cashier-level POS user that cannot issue refunds (POL-01 7.1), and terminal refunds need the manager password, changed from the default on 2026-08-13. On the first Monday of each month the owner checks the processor's refunds report (POL-01 7.7). The tax preparer has read-only access to the accounting SaaS at tax time. There is no outside bookkeeper. Gap: the family member used the owner's POS PIN until the cashier user is set up (P03 G-030, due 2026-09-30).
evidence: POS app user list; processor refunds report; POL-01 7.1 and 7.7; P03 G-030

implementation_statement: The phone locks after 1 minute with a passcode. Gap: the shared family laptop locks after 30 minutes and the store tablet never locks while the POS app is open. Owner sets the laptop to 5 minutes and the tablet to 2 minutes with a PIN.

One Wi-Fi network carries the owner's devices and customers' phones, and its password is printed at the register. The router supports a separate guest network. Owner turns on the guest network for customers, changes the main Wi-Fi password, and stops posting it by 2026-09-30.

No security training. By 2026-10-31 the owner completes a free small-business card security course from the processor's portal and shows the family member how to inspect the terminal and spot phishing and phone scams.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The online store, email, and merchant portal record sign-ins and changes, but nobody looks. Starting 2026-10, on the first Monday of each month the owner checks the online store activity log (logins, add-ons, custom code, checkout settings), the email sign-in history, and the merchant portal refunds report, and notes the check.

Compensating control (one-person business): the owner is the only administrator, so the audit records relied on are kept by the providers, not by the owner. The processor logs terminal activity (P03 G-045), and the online store, email, and merchant portal record sign-ins and changes on the providers' side.
evidence: Processor PCI DSS attestation (requested 2026-08-11); online store activity log; P03 G-045

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner set up, runs, and assessed the controls, and P07 states that independence is limited. The outside IT helper ran the network tests but also set up the router in 2022. POL-01 4.5 requires review by someone outside the store, such as the outside IT helper, at least every second year, with the yearly SAQ evidence kept. The processor's PCI DSS attestation and the website builder's SOC 2 report (P09) cover inherited controls. Base CA-2 is the August self-check.

Compensating control (one-person business): there is no change board, so under CM-3(g) the change control element is the change log. Changes to online store checkout settings, add-ons, custom code, and router settings are written in the change log before they are made, and no add-on or custom code may run on checkout pages (POL-01 7.7). The processor updates the terminal remotely. Gap: no record of changes so far; the change log starts by 2026-10-31 (P03 G-028).

The processor sets and updates the terminal configuration. Owner settings: manual card entry is allowed (needed for phone orders), the router uses factory settings, and the online store custom code setting is open to scripts. Gap: router and terminal defaults not changed before P07 (terminal manager password changed 2026-08-13).
evidence: Router admin page; terminal settings menu; online store settings

implementation_statement: The system list in the company facts (SYS-01 to SYS-10) is the first inventory. Gap: the terminal's make, model, serial number, and location were not recorded, and add-ons and scripts on the online store were not listed.
The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: the family member's open-and-close sheet and the sealed recovery codes are not in place yet (due 2026-12-31).

implementation_statement: The online store, POS app, and accounting vendors back up their own data (inherited; the website builder's backups are described in its SOC 2 report). Owner responsibility: files on the laptop and in the consumer file account have no backup or version history.
evidence: Website builder SOC 2 report; laptop review

implementation_statement: Each vendor service identifies users by account. Gap: the family member signs in to the POS app with the owner's PIN, so sales and voids cannot be told apart. The owner adds a second POS user for the family member by 2026-09-30.

provider_if_inherited: Payment processor; website builder vendor; email provider
implementation_statement: The processor enforces MFA on the merchant portal. Gap: MFA is available but off on the online store administrator account and on the email account that can reset it. Owner turns both on by 2026-09-15.

Passwords are chosen by the owner. Gaps found: the online store password is reused from email; the router administrator password is the label default; the terminal manager password was the factory default until 2026-08-13; the POS PIN is shared. Owner moves to unique passphrases in a password manager by 2026-09-30.
The card data compromise runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-09-04 with a contact list and the processor's 24-hour notice term. Gap: not yet printed or walked through (due 2026-09-30).

Until 2026-08-11, phone-order card numbers, expiration dates, and security codes were written on a paper pad in an unlocked drawer. The 23 pages found were shredded that day. Card details are now keyed while the customer is on the phone and never written down. Remaining step: a locked drawer for any paper with customer details (2026-09-30).
Paper with customer details went into the regular trash. The owner buys a cross-cut shredder by 2026-09-15. Old phones and laptops are to be encrypted, then reset, before trade-in.
The store is locked and alarmed after hours; the owner holds the only keys and alarm code. The tablet is locked in the back room at night. The terminal is in view of the register during open hours.
First risk assessment completed 2026-08-14 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed each August, before each annual SAQ, and after a major change.

The processor is a PCI DSS validated service provider (AOC received 2026-08-12) and the website builder publishes a SOC 2 report (reviewed 2026-08-12). Gap: no list of providers and what each is responsible for, no annual check, and customer data went to a consumer AI chatbot with no business terms.
evidence: Vendor list (planned); AOC; SOC 2 report; P10

implementation_statement: The ISP router blocks unsolicited inbound traffic and the laptop's host firewall is on. Gap: the terminal, tablet, laptop, cameras, and customers' phones share one flat network, so nothing separates the terminal from untrusted devices. Guest network for customers by 2026-09-30; a separate network for the terminal by 2026-12-31.

The terminal encrypts card data to the processor, the hosted payment page and the online store use TLS, and the merchant portal uses TLS (inherited). The owner never sends or accepts card numbers by email or text (POL-01 8.4).

provider_if_inherited: Website builder vendor; POS app vendor
implementation_statement: The vendors encrypt their stored data (website builder SOC 2 report). The phone is encrypted by its passcode. Gap: the shared laptop has no full-disk encryption and holds customer exports; the owner turns on the built-in encryption by 2026-09-15.

provider_if_inherited: Payment processor; device OS vendors; SaaS vendors
implementation_statement: The processor updates the terminal remotely. Automatic OS updates are on for the laptop, phone, and tablet. Gap noted for P01: the router firmware has not been checked since 2022.

The laptop's built-in antivirus runs real-time scanning with automatic updates. Owner responsibility: keep it on and stop family members from turning it off; a separate standard user account for the family is planned (POL-01 9.1).
